And what is God's response to these things? 'You shall say to the sons of Israel:' 'The One who sent me to you.' 'This is my name, and a memorial for eternal generations.' For it is God's nature to exist and be forever. The one who exists and is without beginning and end, and who has not been made, will avoid corruption, and because he does not have his existence from another, he will be testified to by himself. For God is uncreated and unborn, and has the Son who was born from his substance, through whom he also made the ages, and gives existence to those who did not exist, and gives life to all who are capable of living. And again, he illuminates with divine and intellectual light those who need it. And knowing and teaching this, the divine David sings to the Father of all, God, 'You have multiplied your mercy, God, and the sons of men hope in the shadow of your wings.' They will be drunk from the richness of your house, and you will give them to drink from the river of your delights. For with you is the fountain of life, and in your light we will see light.' And indeed, the wise John said, 'The true light, which illuminates every man coming into the world, was.' For the only-begotten Son of God the Father's substance is an exact character, having all the beauty of the Father in himself, and from what he is, he describes the nature of the one who begot him. Therefore, he also said, 'I am in the Father, and the Father is in me.' But when you hear 'Father' and 'Son', do not think of bodies…

And having escaped the notion about these things, consider what is necessary; and understand that our current discussion is not about something that is generated and corrupted; the nature that dominates all things is incorporeal and transcendent; therefore, the mind should depart from bodily things when learning something about God; the divine nature is beyond all bodily substance and is not limited by place or subject to the ideas of shapes; but even when it is said to generate, it does not fall under certain flows or divisions; for the divine nature generates without being divided; it gives birth without being cut off; but if someone wanted to describe the manner of divine generation, they would ask how the divine nature generated; and I would say, without being ashamed, what kind of mind can conceive things beyond the mind, or what kind of word can interpret things beyond words; for the blessed Paul writes that the peace of Christ that surpasses all mind will guard our hearts; and the wisest Solomon shows that such things are ineffable; and even the holy angels, who are far superior to us, are unaware of the manner of the Son's generation, as the blessed Isaiah says, who can describe his generation; and the prophet Habakkuk explains it more clearly

His virtue has covered the heavens. What would it mean to cover the heavens and also the minds of men with virtue, unless the word about Him is greater than the multitude above and the holy orders? Therefore, the birth of Christ is inexpressible to all creation and completely unknowable. Following the divine Scriptures, we see as in a mirror and an enigma, and we say that He was born and coexists eternally in some ways. The examples are small, and we cannot continuously indicate the nature of God and the manner of generation. It is reasonable to think that there is nothing among the things that have happened that is not inferior to the glory of God. Setting forth a sensible type for the theoretical things, we ascend to what is incomparably superior, and as much as possible, we think well, according to what is attainable, going towards the beauty of the divine nature, that the human word and the form that might be conceived to exist in bodies are non-existent and have not been established from anywhere. But the divine and supercosmic offspring, that is, the Son, has been established, being born specifically from the Father who has been established without birth. Let no one be troubled by the difference of words. For we will not accept the arbitrary opinions of certain people who speak from their hearts and not from the mouth of the Lord, as it is written.

Wake up, those intoxicated with their own wine, not knowing things about themselves, boasting to height, speaking against God injustice, as David also says, weaving a spider's web with weak reasonings, deceiving simple souls, placing them in error, and in pits of destruction, the wisdom is not from above, but earthly, psychic, and demonic, what do they say about the Son's coessentiality with the Father, how can the generated be the same as the ungenerated, there is great difference between the words, for the Son is not to be cut off from coessentiality with the Father, no word persuades us that the generated is different from the generator, but if it is believed to be generated in truth, it will be coessential with the generator

If the Father has truly begotten, then the Son has the same nature as the Father, and it is not possible for the Son to be foreign and of a different kind; for if the divine nature has suffered, it would be proven that it has undergone a change, which is impossible for the divine nature; for a human being begets a human being; and each thing that has the power to beget begets something of the same kind and substance; and a human being does not beget a horse, nor does a horse beget a dog; and since God is much greater than us, He will also be greater in this respect, and His Son will be considered to be of the same substance as Himself; for the divine nature does not suffer; if God has created all things in the beginning and has made each thing to be of the same substance as Himself, why would He deprive Himself of this; if it is impossible to think or say this, then it is also impossible to say that the Son is not of the same substance as the Father; if they think that God has not truly begotten the Son, then what is the difference between their words, and why do they try to undermine the glory of the Son, saying that He is of a different substance than the Father; if God has not begotten the Son, then the Son is not begotten at all; therefore, let the question be resolved, and let them stop building a wall of words around us, making a problem out of the difference in words

and if the Father has not begotten, who then is the Only-Begotten, about whom God and Father speaks, saying 'I have begotten you from the womb before the morning star'; for the phrase 'from the womb' is used, since the discussion about these things is made as if about humans, so that from the things among us, we might understand the thing above us, and believe the Son to be born from the Father's substance; I marvel at how, even being very bitter and thinking themselves wise, they have overlooked this; for the divine Paul, being a steward of the divine mysteries for us, and appointed for this purpose, shows that God is the first and only true Father, and that the things that have happened from him are according to likeness to him
pass_b_english: God's response to human inquiry is to reveal his nature and character.
He says, 'You shall tell the sons of Israel that the One who sent me to you is the eternal, uncreated, and unborn God, always in accordance with the nature of the true God.'
This God has a Son who was born from his substance, through whom he made the ages and gives life to all who are capable of living.
He is the fountain of life, and in his light, we see light.
The divine David sings to God, 'You have multiplied your mercy, and the sons of men hope in the shadow of your wings.' (Psalm 36:7-8)
They will be filled with the richness of your house, and you will give them to drink from the river of your delights.
The only-begotten Son of God is an exact character of the Father's substance, having all the beauty of the Father in himself.
He describes the nature of the one who begot him, and he says, 'I am in the Father, and the Father is in me.' (John 14:10-11)
This relationship is not one of physical bodies, but of spiritual unity and co-existence.
The wise John also testifies to this truth, saying, 'The true light, which illuminates every man coming into the world, was.' (John 1:9)
When considering the nature of God, it is essential to transcend the limitations of human understanding and to recognize that the divine nature is beyond all bodily substance.
The mind should depart from bodily things when learning something about God, for the divine nature is not limited by place or subject to the ideas of shapes.
Even when it is said to generate, it does not fall under certain flows or divisions, for the divine nature generates without being divided.
The manner of divine generation is a mystery that surpasses human comprehension, and even the holy angels, who are far superior to us, are unaware of it.
As the blessed Isaiah says, who can describe his generation? (Isaiah 53:8)
The prophet Habakkuk explains it more clearly, but ultimately, it is a truth that is beyond words and beyond the mind.
The peace of Christ that surpasses all mind will guard our hearts.
The virtue of Christ has covered the heavens, and this covering is not just a physical phenomenon, but also a spiritual one, where the minds of men are covered with the virtue of the Son.
This is because the word about Him is greater than the multitude above and the holy orders.
As a result, the birth of Christ is inexpressible to all creation and completely unknowable.
We can only attempt to understand it by following the divine Scriptures, which provide us with a glimpse of the truth, as if we are seeing it as in a mirror and an enigma.
The examples we use to describe the nature of God and the manner of generation are small and insufficient, and we cannot continuously indicate the truth.
However, it is reasonable to think that there is nothing among the things that have happened that is not inferior to the glory of God.

By setting forth a sensible type for the theoretical things, we can ascend to what is incomparably superior, and as much as possible, we think well, according to what is attainable, going towards the beauty of the divine nature.
Those who are intoxicated with their own wine need to wake up, for they are boasting about their own accomplishments and speaking against God's justice, as the prophet David also says.
They are foolishly weaving a web of deceit with their weak reasonings, and in doing so, they are deceiving simple souls and placing them in error and in pits of destruction.
The wisdom they claim to have is not from above, but rather it is earthly, psychic, and demonic.
They attempt to explain the coessentiality of the Son with the Father, but their words are empty and lacking in truth.
For how can the generated be the same as the ungenerated?
There is a great difference between these concepts, and no word can persuade us that the generated is different from the generator.
However, if it is believed that the Son is truly generated, then He will be coessential with the Father.
If the Father has truly begotten the Son, then it is only logical that the Son shares the same nature as the Father.
It is impossible for the Son to be foreign and of a different kind, for this would imply that the divine nature has undergone a change, which is utterly impossible.
The very notion of begetting implies a shared nature, as seen in the human experience where a human being begets another human being.
Each thing that has the power to beget produces something of the same kind and substance, and it is absurd to suggest that a human being could beget a horse or a horse beget a dog.
Given God's greatness, it is only fitting that His Son would be of the same substance as Himself.
The divine nature does not suffer or undergo change, and it is impossible to think or say otherwise.
If God has created all things in the beginning and has made each thing to be of the same substance as Himself, why would He deprive Himself of this same substance?
If it is impossible to conceive of God in this way, then it is also impossible to suggest that the Son is not of the same substance as the Father.

Those who argue that God has not truly begotten the Son must explain the difference between their words and why they seek to undermine the glory of the Son by claiming that He is of a different substance than the Father.
Ultimately, if God has not begotten the Son, then the Son is not begotten at all, and the question should be resolved once and for all.
Let no one be troubled by the difference of words, for we will not accept the arbitrary opinions of certain people who speak from their hearts and not from the mouth of the Lord, as it is written.

Wake up, those intoxicated with their own wine, not knowing things about themselves, boasting to height, speaking against God injustice, as David also says, weaving a spider's web with weak reasonings, deceiving simple souls, placing them in error, and in pits of destruction, the wisdom is not from above, but earthly, psychic, and demonic, what do they say about the Son's coessentiality with the Father, how can the generated be the same as the ungenerated, there is great difference between the words, for the Son is not to be cut off from coessentiality with the Father, no word persuades us that the generated is different from the generator, but if it is believed to be generated in truth, it will be coessential with the generator.
Let no one be troubled by the difference of words, for we will not accept the arbitrary opinions of certain people who speak from their hearts and not from the mouth of the Lord, as it is written.
